title: First Blood at Boavista: Baker Runs Away, Mullin Rewrites the Record
title_candidates: First Blood at Boavista: Baker Runs Away, Mullin Rewrites the Record
Eighteen Shots Clear, and Still Only the Second-Best Story
theme: A tournament of firsts on one much-abused parkland course: Jon Baker's maiden Trophy, taken from the front and never once threatened, while everyone else — Mullin included — set personal bests, a course record and a small museum of blow-ups on Boavista's supposedly harmless 17th.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, insider ribbing; Barney Ronay by way of Tom Peck
opening_hook: Act I opens on the R1 scoring hut at Boavista, where two TEG records fell in the same afternoon (Baker's -9, Mullin's +17 gross) and Henry Meller signed for a 12 at the 17th — all three competitions effectively cast in a single round, which the rest of the report then explains.
foreshadow: Boavista's 17th — stroke index 17, the second-easiest hole on the card — begins collecting victims from R1 and does not stop.
Jon Baker's R1 90 gross is 10 better than anything he had ever managed here and 17 better than his last visit: the handicap is about to be looted.
David Mullin arrives as defending Trophy champion and the best gross player in the field — and will end up owning the course record and still losing the main event by 18.
Henry Meller arrives as reigning Wooden Spoon holder, then posts one of the best rounds in TEG history in R2.

competitions.name: Trophy (Net VP)
competitions.how: Baker's opening -9 (b03), the best round in TEG history to date and built on a 90 gross that was 10 shots better than any previous Boavista effort of his, gave him an 8-shot lead after R1. The only lead change of the entire Trophy came at R1 H6 (Mullin, not outright, routine) — after that Baker was never headed across 66 holes. He widened it to 13 with R2's -2 (b07) despite bleeding shots through the turn, to 16 with R3's -7 (b08) — a round that also contained a 9 at the 18th (b19) and a quadruple at the 5th, and still gained ground — and closed out level par in R4 (b21 stretch, b40) for an 18-shot margin, 9th-best Trophy score all-time and a first TEG title.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.how: Mullin took gross command at R1 H4 (b02: +17, the best gross round in TEG history to date) and led the Jacket wire-to-wire: 2 clear after R1, 5 after R2, 9 after R3, 12 at the finish over Stuart Neumann. The signature act was R3's 85 gross (cr01, b04) — a new Boavista course record, beating the 89 that had stood across 15 prior visits, and his own personal best here by 4. His only real blemishes were a 9 at the 17th in R2 (b18) and a quadruple at the 11th in R4 (b24), neither of which cost him a thing.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.winner_or_loser: Henry Meller — loser at +16 net VP
competitions.how: Meller's Spoon was booked twice. First in R1, when a 12 at the 17th (b06) — the worst hole relative to par in TEG history to date, on stroke index 17 — dropped him outright to the bottom (b61). He then produced the escape act of the tournament in R2: -2 and 89 gross (b12, b13), a personal Boavista best, lifting him to 3rd. R3 undid all of it inside three holes: a triple at the 1st put him back to the bottom (b27), Gregg Williams's quadruple at the 2nd briefly took it off him (b28), and Meller's 10 at the 3rd (b22) returned him to last (b29) for good. A +4 in R4, complete with an 8 at the 7th (b38), confirmed back-to-back Spoons.

rounds.chosen_headline: Meller's Finest Hour, Baker's Quiet Larceny
rounds.angle: Meller posts a career Boavista best (b12, b13) and climbs to 3rd; Baker still extends to 13 with a -2 (b07) that included five straight doubles; the 17th takes Mullin (b18).

headline_candidates: The Spoon Changes Hands Three Times in Three Holes
A Course Record, and a Man Nine Shots Worse Off at the Last
rounds.angle: The centrepiece round — Mullin's course-record 85 (cr01, b04, b11) against a Spoon race that swaps owner at H1, H2 and H3 (b27, b28, b29) — while Baker shrugs off a 9 at the 18th (b19) and still gains three.

headline_candidates: Baker Coasts, Neumann Detonates, Williams Files His Quadruples
Level Par Is Quite Enough, Thank You
rounds.angle: Nothing left to decide but plenty left to survive: Baker's level-par lap seals -18 (b01), Mullin's 20 confirms the Jacket (b05), Neumann's 10 at the 17th (b17) closes the motif, and Meller signs for the Spoon (b20).

players.arc: Runner-up in TEG 2 and with no titles to his name, Baker opened with the best round in TEG history, led from R1 H6 to the final putt, and turned a 90 gross — 17 shots better than his previous visit to Boavista — into a first Trophy by a preposterous 18.

The defending champion played the best golf in the field by any raw measure — two TEG-record gross rounds and a course-record 85 — and was comprehensively beaten on the metric that hands out the Trophy.
Reigning Spoon holder who set a personal Boavista best in R2 and still contrived to lose the Spoon race twice, the second time inside three holes of R3.
Quietly the second-best gross player of the tournament, briefly bottom of the Spoon race in R2, and author of the final indignity at the 17th.
Improved his Boavista best by eight shots to 97 while simultaneously compiling the tournament's fullest catalogue of quadruple bogeys — and spent two holes of R3 as the Spoon incumbent.

venue_notes: All four rounds at Boavista Golf & Spa Resort, Lagos — the 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th TEG rounds at the venue and TEG's 2nd trip to the Algarve. Use Howard Swan's parkland-with-Atlantic-views and the course's two distinct halves early, then let the course become an accounting exercise: everyone in the field posted a new personal best here, and the record that had stood across 15 prior visits fell in R3. The running venue gag is the 17th — a par 4 ranked stroke index 17, the second-easiest hole on the card — which took a 12, a 9 and a 10 off three different players across the four days.
course_history_notes: Every one of the five set a new personal best at Boavista on his 4th visit — a field-wide reappraisal of a course TEG had already played three times.
Jon Baker's R1 90 gross beat his prior Boavista best of 100 (TEG 2) by 10, and was 17 shots better than his last visit.
Gregg Williams's R3 97 was 8 better than his previous Boavista best of 105 (TEG 2).
David Mullin's R3 85 (cr01) beat both his own prior best of 89 and the Boavista course record of 89 that had survived 15 prior visits.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R1's -9 (b03) — Baker outright ahead by 8 after one round, and never headed again across the remaining 66 holes; by R3 (b08) the lead was 16 and the argument was over.
Green Jacket: R1 H4 (b02) — Mullin ahead on gross and gone, the 85 course record in R3 (cr01) turning a 5-shot cushion into 9 and rendering R4 ceremonial.
Wooden Spoon: R3 H3 (b29) — Meller's 10 at the 3rd (b22) returned him to the bottom for the final time, three holes after R2 had lifted him clear of it.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Kept as a supporting vehicle — both wire-to-wire arcs are real and drive the telling — but the frame is Baker's first-ever Trophy (origin), with the field's blow-up inventory as catalogue; inevitability can't be prominent by rule and shouldn't be, since a maiden win by 18 is a story about arrival, not procession.
